claims.text: The FOMC decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

citations.quotation: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4 percent

claims.text: Neel Kashkari dissented, preferring to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.

citations.quotation: Voting against the action was Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.

claims.text: A key uncertainty about the future policy path is inflation: the Committee expects inflation to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term and is monitoring inflation developments closely, while the pace of future adjustments depends on realized and expected economic conditions.

citations.quotation: Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced, but the Committee is monitoring inflation developments closely.

claims.text: The Committee will base the timing and size of future rate adjustments on an assessment of realized and expected economic conditions relative to its objectives.

citations.quotation: In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions

counterarguments.text: A counterpoint to the rate hike is that inflation remained soft — market-based measures of inflation compensation were low and inflation was expected to stay below 2 percent near term — which is the implied concern behind Kashkari's dissent to hold rates steady. The dissent itself is the cited opposing evidence in the document.

citations.quotation:
Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of
longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.

limitations: The source excerpts are partial; the full statement is not provided.
